mutations.after:
trap - INT TERM EXIT
  if [ -n "$run_hb_pid" ]; then
mutations.because: the old order in run_cleanup: `trap - INT TERM EXIT` restores the DEFAULT disposition and so undoes the `trap '' INT TERM` forward_signal had installed, which leaves a second TERM free to kill the shell at any point in the cleanup — before release, with the lock still at the name. The window is the cleanup's `wait` for the heartbeat loop, and a refresh parked in CF_GATE_TEST_PAUSE_BEFORE_BEAT_MV keeps that loop from exiting until the test removes the marker, so the second signal can be sent there rather than hoping to hit a race: one TERM, 500ms, a second TERM, and the lock must still be released. Without the ordering the shell is gone before the release runs — exit 143, no `released by` line, and the lock left behind with all four of its files while a heartbeat grandchild keeps refreshing a dead holder's beat. Measured on /bin/sh and /bin/dash before the fix.
command: a second signal while the release is waiting on the loop

mutations.because: is_slot_path is the whole of what a slot NAME is: `cf-gate.lock`, or `cf-gate.lock.<n>` with n matching [1-9] or [1-9][0-9] and BELOW MAX_SLOTS (0..63 at a ceiling of 64). This mutation restores the rule it replaced — any suffix starting with a digit — which is the `cf-gate.lock.[0-9]*` glob the function exists to replace, and a slot's own transients are named after the slot, so `cf-gate.lock.1.cand.999` and `cf-gate.lock.1.reclaim.999.x` both begin with a digit and become slots 1, twice over. That is not a cosmetic listing: existing_slots feeds caller_slot, pid_slot and self_held_slot as well as status, so a paused creator's or reclaimer's directory becomes a candidate lock to release, heartbeat or refuse an acquire over. The status test plants all four transient names as real directories holding all four lock files and asserts that status names every real slot and none of them, at CF_GATE_SLOTS=1 so a numbered path can only surface through the scan's own filter. Both halves of the rule are in the replaced text and both have to go: `[ "1.cand.999" -lt 64 ]` is not a comparison any shell can make, it answers false, and a false answer there is a REFUSAL — so relaxing only the shape leaves the transients rejected and this claim does not reproduce. Measured, this round: with the shape alone mutated the status test still passed (verdict: survived).
command: status lists every slot that exists

mutations.before:
trap - EXIT
  trap '' INT TERM
  release_lock
mutations.because: the same defect in gate.sh's cleanup, and the reason the gate's own line is the assertion rather than the lock's absence: release_lock's release is a CHILD process, and a child outlives a parent that is signal-killed. With the default TERM action restored, a second TERM during the release killed the gate before it printed `gate: lock released, heartbeat stopped`, and the orphaned child then removed the lock anyway — a gate that reported neither the release nor its failure. The test parks that release between its owner/pid check and the removal (CF_GATE_TEST_PAUSE_BEFORE_RELEASE), sends the second TERM there, and asserts exit 143 with the line printed; parking the heartbeat cannot hold this window open because gate.sh's loop has TERM at default and dies at once.

Dropping is_slot_path from existing_slots removes the canonical-name rule from the SCAN, leaving only "it is a directory" and "this user owns it" — and both of those pass for a name no acquirer could ever have produced. The test plants `cf-gate.lock.0` and `cf-gate.lock.007`, each holding the real holder's owner and pid (a forgery that did not match would never get that far) and each sorting BEFORE the real slot 1, and asserts that an unpinned status does not list them, that an unpinned heartbeat refreshes slot 1 rather than `.0`, and that neither planted directory is touched. This is the unpinned caller: only CF_GATE_CALLER_PID, no CF_GATE_SLOT_PATH — the same shape as a caller that did not come from an acquire. `/tmp` is 1777, so at SLOTS>1 a directory that sorts before a real slot is something any local user can write.
command: a planted slot name that is not canonical

mutations.because: Provenance is what makes a planted directory unusable, and `[ -d "$1" ]` is what is left without it: a symlink to a directory passes -d (it follows the link), and the uid test cannot see the difference because `find` on a symlink start point reports the LINK's owner and never descends. The uid seam (CF_GATE_TEST_EXPECT_UID) is the same filter seen from the other side: a slot this user owns is not a lock once the expected uid is somebody else's, and the pinned path answers exit 2 for a pin that fails it.

A pin is the whole fix — the slot the acquire took, handed back to the loop that refreshes it — and `run` pins in-process for exactly this call, the same way gate.sh does for its own.
